title: Day 724 — Attorney General Godoy Fires FGR Guanajuato Delegate Over 'Anomalies' in the September Fuel-Seizure Case
detail: Attorney General Ernestina Godoy removed FGR delegate Juan Francisco Vera Ayala from his post in Guanajuato, Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch confirmed at Sheinbaum's September 25, 2026 (Day 724, Friday) mañanera in Villahermosa, Tabasco, after the FGR's own team detected "certain anomalies" in the investigation behind the record 59-million-liter fuel-theft seizure the Security Cabinet had touted on September 18. The removal followed a roughly two-week gap between the early-September operation and its public announcement during Sheinbaum's Guanajuato tour stop, which had raised questions about the case's handling. Harfuch said the case remains under investigation and did not implicate Pemex personnel. The episode adds to Sheinbaum's broader anti-huachicol and anti-corruption push, which her government says has led to 2,654 arrests for fuel theft since October 2024.

media.caption: FGR delegate in Guanajuato removed after anomalies found in the record 59-million-liter fuel-theft seizure case

title: Day 724 — Sheinbaum Says Juchitán Mayor's Extortion Arrest Is Not Linked to Attack on Designer Elvis Guerra, Contradicting Oaxaca Governor
detail: President Sheinbaum said at her September 25, 2026 mañanera that the September 23 detention of Juchitán de Zaragoza mayor Miguel Sánchez Altamirano — arrested by Navy, federal and state forces alongside an alleged accomplice on outstanding warrants for aggravated extortion and crimes against state security, with the UIF freezing his accounts — is not related to the armed attack on muxe fashion designer Elvis Guerra, who made the dress Sheinbaum wore at the September 15 Grito de Independencia. Sheinbaum said the arrest stemmed from a longer-running organized-crime investigation into extortion and protection-money collection from local merchants, even though it came days after Guerra's attack complaint. Her account directly contradicted Oaxaca Governor Salomón Jara, who had said the mayor's arrest was tied to the attack on Guerra, who had reported escalating extortion threats — including an August demand for 200,000 pesos — before the assault.

media.caption: Sheinbaum addresses the detention of Juchitán mayor Miguel Sánchez Altamirano and the attack on designer Elvis Guerra

title: Day 724 — Tabasco Tour Stop: Sheinbaum Touts Crime-Rate Drop, Declines Meeting With Andy López Beltrán Amid His US Visa Revocation
detail: Sheinbaum held her September 25, 2026 mañanera from Villahermosa, Tabasco, where Governor Javier May Rodríguez thanked her for the visit and highlighted scholarships, social programs and cacao-producer support. SESNSP executive secretary Marcela Figueroa Franco presented state security data showing Tabasco's daily average of high-impact crimes fell 18% (from 12.6 to 10.3) and homicidios dolosos dropped 54% since the administration's national security strategy took effect, with vehicle theft down 51% versus November 2024. Asked about Andrés Manuel López Beltrán — the former president's son, whose U.S. visa the State Department revoked in August, prompting a letter from López Beltrán accusing Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Christopher Landau of acting "like gang bosses" — Sheinbaum called the revocation "a political matter, it has nothing to do with anything else," said any accusations against Mexican citizens should come with evidence presented to Mexican authorities, and ruled out meeting him during the Tabasco visit while saying his territorial work ahead of a 2027 federal deputy run looks "very well" to her.

media.caption: Sheinbaum tours Tabasco, touts falling crime rates and declines to meet Andy López Beltrán amid his revoked US visa
